## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`select_failures` needs a fix before merge: it compares report paths to `requested` without the `normalize` step that `select_explicit` uses, so a failed test the report lists as `./tests/...` never gets selected. This review read both changed files in full, traced the new selector against `normalize` and `select_explicit` in `app/selection.py`, and read the three added tests. It did not run them. The `select_cached` and `_select_normalized` rewrites behave the same as the code they replace.

## Changes
The pull request adds `select_failures`, which picks requested paths out of a runner report's `failed` list. It also rewrites `select_cached` and `_select_normalized` without changing their behavior, and adds `tests/test_selection.py` covering the explicit, cached and failure-report selectors.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/selection.py:20 — correctness — Normalize report paths before matching in select_failures — A report of `{"failed": ["./tests/test_x.py"]}` with `requested={"tests/test_x.py"}` returns `[]` rather than `["./tests/test_x.py"]`. The comparison is a raw `path in requested`. The docstring promises the same contract as `select_explicit` (line 6), "preserving its original spelling", and `select_explicit` keeps the original spelling while matching on `normalize(path) in requested`. The added test at tests/test_selection.py:13 only uses paths without the `./` prefix, so it can't catch this. — Any runner that reports failures with a `./` prefix, such as pytest run as `pytest ./tests`, gets those failed tests silently left out of the selection, so they don't re-run. — Fix: Use `[path for path in report["failed"] if normalize(path) in requested]` to match `select_explicit`, and add a test with a `./`-prefixed report entry.
